title: observability: token-level KV cache metrics, cost/latency breakdowns, dashboards and alert tuning
author: Priya Rao
body:
Motivation: operators asked for more granular insight into per-request token costs and how KV cache hits/misses impact latency and unit economics (see ENG-3421). This PR collects token-level cost and latency breakdowns for requests, surfaces KV cache hit/miss metrics, adds tracing spans for KV cache lookup hot paths, and ships dashboards + tuned alerts to reduce noisy paging incidents.

Summary of changes: 1) Add token-level counters and histograms (per-model, per-route) for generated tokens, input tokens, and inferred cost at the request level. 2) Instrument KV cache with hit/miss counters and per-operation latency histograms; emit tags for cache tier (local/remote) and shard. 3) Add tracing spans around cache lookup, cache population, and fallback model routing. 4) Dashboard and alerting: new Grafana dashboard (Token-level Cost & KV Cache) with cost/latency waterfalls, p50/p90/p99 token latency breakdowns, KV hit-rate heatmaps, and per-model cost trend panels. 5) Alert tuning: replace a noisy incident rule with a two-stage alert (warning -> critical) and add rate-limited escalation for global kv_miss spikes. 6) Tests and perf: add unit tests for aggregation logic and a small microbenchmark showing <=3% p95 overhead on representative workloads.

Checklist:
- [x] Metrics + histograms implemented and emitted
- [x] Tracing spans added and integrated with existing trace service
- [x] Dashboards created and linked in Console
- [x] Alerts tuned with noise reduction and escalation
- [x] Unit tests added for aggregation/rollup code
- [x] Performance microbenchmark added and recorded

Testing and rollout notes: Metrics are behind a feature flag (observability.token_level_enabled) and default to OFF in main to avoid immediate cardinality impact; rollout plan: enable for 10% of traffic for 48h, validate storage and dashboard panels, then gradual ramp to 100% if no storage or cost regressions. Alert thresholds are conservative and use relative baseline (5x baseline kv_miss rate sustained for 5m -> warning; 10x for 2m -> critical).

Related: references ENG-3421, PM-198, SUP-129. See dashboards and alert rules under redwood/observability/dashboards/token_cost_kv/* for JSON panels and redwood/observability/alerts/kv_alerts.yaml for rule definitions.

Notes for reviewers: focus on aggregation correctness, potential cardinality concerns, and whether the alert thresholds are gated well enough. I included simple sampling and label pruning (model_name -> top-10 tag + other) to limit cardinality.

4d5e6f7: perf: add microbenchmark for metrics emission path and CI job to run it
8f9a0b1: observability: add Grafana dashboard JSON and alert rules; feature flag and rollout docs
files_changed: redwood/observability/metrics/token_metrics.go - add token counters, histograms, and attribution helpers (approx +220 lines)
redwood/observability/kv/kv_metrics.go - instrument KV cache hit/miss counters, latency histograms, and tags for tier/shard
redwood/serving/runtime/cache_lookup.go - add tracing spans around cache lookup/populate and attach cache metadata to traces
redwood/observability/dashboards/token_cost_kv/dashboard.json - Grafana dashboard with token cost waterfall, per-model panels, and KV hit-rate heatmaps
redwood/observability/alerts/kv_alerts.yaml - new alert rules with warning/critical stages and rate-limiting annotations
redwood/config/feature_flags.yaml - add observability.token_level_enabled flag and rollout config
redwood/observability/tests/token_metrics_test.go - unit tests for aggregation and tag rollup logic
infra/ci/microbench/jobs.yaml - add job to run metrics emission microbench on CI runners
review_comments: Ethan Wang (reviewer): Can you explain how you prevent high-cardinality explosion when instrumenting per-model token metrics? Suggest limiting to top-k models and sampling.
Priya Rao (author): Implemented top-10 tag rollup and sampling; added explicit note in config and tests to verify tag pruning. See token_metrics.go lines 120-160.
Liam O'Connor (reviewer): The initial alert rule caused a noisy page in staging yesterday (SUP-129). Can we add suppression and a two-stage alert?
Priya Rao (author): Updated kv_alerts.yaml to add warning/critical stages, 5m/2m windows respectively, and a runbook link. Also added rate-limited annotations to avoid escalation storms.
Sofia Chen (reviewer): Please add a unit test for aggregation when the number of unique models exceeds the configured top-k. Also confirm the microbench shows acceptable overhead for p95.

Priya Rao (author): Added token_metrics_test.go covering rollup and a microbench with CI gating; benchmark results included in PR description artifacts and summarized in the related Linear item (ENG-3421).
release_notes: Added token-level cost and latency metrics, KV cache hit/miss instrumentation, dashboards for token cost and KV metrics, and tuned alerts to reduce noise. Feature gated behind observability.token_level_enabled; rollout plan included.
additional_notes: CI: first run had a flaky microbench failure due to runner load; retriggered and all checks passed (full CI green).
Performance: measured <=3% p95 overhead on the emission path for representative workloads (see microbench artifact).
Rollout: Admins should monitor storage and cardinality for first 48h after enabling. Default OFF in main to allow deliberate rollout.
